gate: the candidate may not introduce a decision the baseline never produced, on any case of the frozen turn corpus. A variant that invents one decision is rejected however much it saves. Cases that are nondeterministic inside a single arm are reported rather than hidden, because a set comparison alone would overstate the gate.
method: the real sidecar per variant, whole sessions alternated in ABBA order, the same 12-case corpus twice per session. The candidate removes the two fields from the schema and BAXY fills them back in from mode and effect_operations, so everything downstream sees the identical decision shape.

verdict.status: REJECTED. Not promoted; production is unchanged.
verdict.what_broke: guard-04 ('podrias dejarme la pantalla lista para trabajar') decided conversation deterministically in the baseline. With the cleaned prompt it sometimes decided clarify, asking '¿Que aplicacion deseas abrir?'. The case also went from deterministic to nondeterministic.
verdict.likely_cause: the removed text included 'operation debe estar vacio salvo en action, donde debe coincidir con el unico elemento de effect_operations'. That sentence anchored the idea that a non-action turn carries no operation. Removing it loosened that anchor even though the field itself no longer exists.
verdict.value_it_would_have_bought: essentially nothing: -0.72 emitted tokens. Those sentences live in the cached system prefix, so they cost almost no prefill (332.7 -> 326.3 ms) and no decode. The -152.5 ms p50 decode delta is not attributable to the change, since the token count barely moved; it is session noise.
verdict.lesson: this looked obviously safe: it deleted instructions about two fields that no longer exist in the schema. It still moved a decision. Prompt text that describes a removed field can still be carrying semantics for a field that remains.
